text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday . Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- The presidents of Ukraine, Poland and the three Baltic states met in Tallinn yesterday. They approved a joint communique, which stresses the need for increased stability and security in Europe and calls for NATO to stay open for all membership seekers.
SONUMILEHT
- The government discussed a draft law on the wages of civil servants. The draft aims at raising the wages and reducing the share of various extra payments.
- The government supported the idea of a Freedom Monument to be built in Tallinn and charged the culture ministry with responsibility for the preparations.
- An Estonian infantry platoon is participating in a NATO exercise Cooperative Banners in Norway.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- Conflict continues in the village of Simuna over a drunkard, who died after having been transported in the luggage compartment of a police car.
- At least six elementary schools and one basic school will be closed down by the autumn. The closing of more schools is predicted for the future because of a low birth rate.
POSTIMEES
- Central prison officials may be charged with corruption.
- Top officials are suspected of involvement in shady business deals.
- The Estonian army received $2.8 million of U.S. military equipment, including communications devices and medical supplies.
- A delegation of St Petersburg journalists is touring Estonia. They have already visited south Estonia and will reach Tallinn on Friday.
ARIPAEV
- The share of bootleg vodka has increased to 43.6 percent of the total market. Distillers call for a law on alcohol to reduce the sale of illegally produced or imported vodka.
- The Tourism Board predicts tourism income to reach 8.5 billion kroons this year and 12 billion next year.
- Hansapank, Savings Bank, Forexbank and Tallinna Pank plan to introduce a common Cirrus/Maestro bank card this summer.
